cards.explanation: The answer is a bride's love. The LORD says, “I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride…” (Jeremiah 2:2). Before any hard words, the first thing out of His mouth is the good part. A bride's love is the kind that follows you somewhere with no map and not one cookie.

The answer is False. The LORD remembers how Israel followed Him “…in the wilderness, in a land not sown.” (Jeremiah 2:2). A land not sown means no planted fields at all. The statement said planted fields, and the verse says the opposite.

The answer is that they were found guilty. The verse says, “All who devoured her were found guilty; disaster came upon them…” (Jeremiah 2:3). The verse just before that calls Israel holy to the LORD. Anyone who went after her in those days ended up answering for it.

The answer is what fault they found in Him. He asks, “What fault did your fathers find in Me that they strayed so far from Me?” (Jeremiah 2:5). I think that question stings, because it asks them to name what went wrong. It's all about why they strayed from Him.

The answer is worthless. “They followed worthless idols, and became worthless themselves.” (Jeremiah 2:5). The fathers followed worthless idols first. After that, the verse says they became worthless themselves.

The answer is “Where is the LORD who brought us up from the land of Egypt…” (Jeremiah 2:6). That's the question the LORD says they did not ask. He had led them through the wilderness, and still they did not ask where He was. I think that missing question is what makes His words sting.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “…you came and defiled My land and made My inheritance detestable.” (Jeremiah 2:7). He had brought them into a fertile land, and they defiled it. So they did not keep it holy.

The answer is True. The verse says, “The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed useless idols.” (Jeremiah 2:8). Baal was a false god, and the prophets spoke in his name. So the priests, the leaders and the prophets all turned from the LORD.

The answer is False. The LORD says He will “…bring a case against your children’s children.” (Jeremiah 2:9). So His case isn't only about the people living right then. It reaches to the generations after them too.

The answer is that a nation changed its gods. The LORD asks, “Has a nation ever changed its gods?” (Jeremiah 2:11). He sends them out to look at the coasts of Cyprus and to Kedar, a desert tribe, and to see if anything like this has happened. Even people with gods that aren't gods at all stay loyal to them.

The answer is useless idols. The LORD says, “…My people have exchanged their Glory for useless idols.” (Jeremiah 2:11). They gave up their Glory and took idols the verse calls useless. That's a trade nobody should want.
The answer is False. He tells the heavens, “Be stunned by this, O heavens; be shocked and utterly appalled…” (Jeremiah 2:12). Singing for joy isn't in the verse. Being shocked is.

The answer is the fountain of living water. The LORD says, “They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water…” (Jeremiah 2:13). A fountain keeps flowing, and that's what they walked away from. Walking away from a fountain is a strange way to handle being thirsty.

The answer is False. The LORD calls them “…broken cisterns that cannot hold water.” (Jeremiah 2:13). They dug these themselves, and they don't work. Same as me trying to bake with a stamper that has no edges left, which gives you a smudge and a sad face.

The answer is young lions. The LORD says, “The young lions have roared at him; they have sounded their voices.” (Jeremiah 2:15). Israel has become prey, and the lions are the ones roaring. I think this is a heavy picture.
The answer is False. The verse says, “his cities lie in ruins, without inhabitant.” (Jeremiah 2:15). Nobody is living in them. A town like that doesn't have a single person to wave at you.

The answer is Israel himself. The LORD asks, “Have you not brought this on yourself by forsaking the LORD your God when He led you in the way?” (Jeremiah 2:17). He asks whether Israel brought this on himself by forsaking Him. The question points right back at Israel.

The answer is the Nile. The LORD asks, “…what will you gain on your way to Egypt to drink the waters of the Nile?” (Jeremiah 2:18). He asks the same thing about the Euphrates on the way to Assyria. Two roads, two rivers, and one question about what Israel gains.

The answer is True. The Lord GOD of Hosts says, “Consider and realize how evil and bitter it is for you to forsake the LORD your God and to have no fear of Me…” (Jeremiah 2:19). He wants them to stop and really think about it. Sometimes you need to look at what you've done with both eyes open.
